title: Parse minutes into a result
prompt: `Parsed` is supplied. Write `public static Parsed ParseMinutes(string text)`. When `text` is a whole number of 0 or more, return `Parsed` with `Ok` true, that number, and an empty `Error`. When `text` is not a number representable by int, return `Ok` false, 0 and the `Error` `"not a number"`. When it is a negative number, return `Ok` false, 0 and the `Error` `"negative"`. The method must not throw for any of these.
hints: Bad text and out-of-range numbers are both unsuccessful parses. Which API reports those without throwing?
Use int.TryParse before testing whether the parsed number is negative.
If TryParse returns false, return Parsed(false, 0, "not a number"). Otherwise reject negative minutes, keeping zero as a valid result.
checkLabels: "0" is a valid number and must give Ok true with 0.
"soon" must give Ok false with the error "not a number".
Empty text must give Ok false with the error "not a number".
"-5" must give Ok false with the error "negative".
Text outside the int range must return not a number without throwing.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Never checks the number after parsing it.

feedback: Go through the three outcomes with the failing text. Check which one your code picks and that all three values of the result match the prompt.
